title: Autosurgeon commit protocol: idempotent SDK client + replay-safe webhooks for Optimize recommendations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Deliver an idempotent, battle-tested commit protocol and SDK primitives that allow Optimize to apply batching/caching recommendations safely. The work includes: 1) a small-footprint client library (TS + Go) that generates stable mutation tokens and performs exactly-once commit semantics; 2) new webhook delivery semantics (at-least-once with idempotency-key, sequence numbers, and replay detection) plus a dry-run reconcile endpoint for safe previews; 3) server-side fencing to avoid double-apply and to enable safe automated rollback/compensating transaction execution. Goals: eliminate duplicate recommendation application, make rollbacks deterministic, and give platform teams an ergonomic SDK to integrate into automation pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: SDK: typescript and go clients expose a CommittableApply API with (mutation_token, precondition, dry_run) options and unit tests covering duplicate-retry scenarios
Server: control-plane accepts apply requests with 'mutation_token' and returns deterministic outcome codes (applied | already_applied | precondition_failed | conflict)
Webhooks: recommendation webhooks include idempotency-key, sequence-number, and replay-window headers; delivery logs show safe replays handled without double-apply
Dry-run: /reconcile/dry-run endpoint returns diff + risk-score and a canonical plan id that can be passed to the SDK for guaranteed apply of the same plan
Rollback: automatic compensating operations can be triggered by plan id; rollback is tested end-to-end in staging with simulated flaky delivery and node restarts
Observability: per-plan tracing (trace id), Prometheus metrics for duplicate-apply attempts, and a dashboard showing apply/retry/failure rates
Security: all mutation tokens are signed and validated; KMS key rotation tested; security review completed
design_decisions: Use a client-generated mutation_token (v1: HMAC of plan id + timestamp + client id) to avoid server state for every inflight attempt
Server will persist the canonical plan outcome keyed by mutation_token for idempotent lookups; entry TTL of 30 days
Webhooks remain at-least-once delivery; idempotency guaranteed by mutation_token + sequence-number; receivers must be able to ignore older sequence numbers
Dry-run endpoint produces a deterministic plan id (sha256 of normalized plan + server-salt) that the SDK can submit for an exact apply
Fallback behaviour: when a precondition conflict occurs (concurrent manual change), server returns precondition_failed and produces a reconciliation diff for operator review
Do not require distributed transactions across external systems; instead rely on compensating actions and clear audit trails
implementation_notes: Server schema additions: mutation_tokens table (token, plan_id, outcome, applied_at, meta)
API changes: POST /optimize/apply { plan_id, mutation_token, dry_run=false, precondition_hash } -> { status, plan_id, trace_id }
Webhook changes: add headers X-Optimize-Idempotency, X-Optimize-Seq, X-Optimize-Plan-Id and replay window headers
SDK: CommittableApply(ctx, plan, opts) returns (applied bool, status string, server_trace string); retries use exponential backoff with jitter and stop when server returns already_applied
Backfills: a one-time migration to populate existing recommendations with synthetic mutation_tokens for replay safety during rollout
Storage TTL and GC: token entries older than 30 days are GC'd; implement a tombstone state for long-running rollbacks
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy server handling but keep default apply=legacy; enable new endpoints behind feature flag for 5% of traffic
Phase 2 (SDK pilot): ship TS SDK to a small set of internal teams and run end-to-end tests applying recommendations to a staging dedicated account
Phase 3 (gradual): flip feature flag to 25%/50%/100% across clusters, monitor metrics for duplicate-applies and precondition failures
Phase 4 (deprecate): after 4 weeks of stable telemetry, remove legacy apply path and enforce mutation_token validation
Rollback strategy: quick toggle to feature-flag off, and an emergency compensating worker that scans applied plans and reverts using recorded inverse-operations
test_plan: Unit tests for SDK: duplicate send, random reorder, network retry, token tampering
Integration tests in CI: simulate at-least-once webhook delivery with Hermes and verify exactly-once semantics
Chaos tests: kill control-plane nodes during apply and validate idempotent outcomes
Staging e2e: 1000 recommendation applies with injected network flakiness, validate no duplicates and successful rollbacks
Security tests: token signature fuzzing and KMS key rotation scenario
monitoring_playbook: Alert: >5 duplicate-apply attempts per minute for a tenant -> P0 on-call
Alert: spike in precondition_failed rate -> investigate config drift or conflicting manual changes
Runbook: for emergency revert, set feature flag off, then run compensating worker with plan_id list from trace and push rollback PRs to the config repo
SLOs: 99.9% successful apply within 10s for committed plans (excluding dry-run)
Dashboard: 'Optimize Apply' showing applies, already_applied, retries, failures, avg latency, and top failing tenants
blockers: Need final sign-off on mutation_token format from security (KMS implications)
Telemetry: require new tracing headers schema to be accepted by observability team for per-plan traces
SDK ownership: allocate an engineer to maintain both TS and Go SDKs post-launch
